doc.title: # Training history · {from} to {to}
doc.range: Requested period: {from} to {to}. There are sets from {first} to {last}, on {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ({sets, plural, one {# set} other {# sets}}, {exercises, plural, one {# exercise} other {# exercises}}). A day without sets doesn't confirm rest: it may just not have been logged.
doc.rangeEmpty: Requested period: {from} to {to}. No sets logged in this period.
doc.measurementsNote: Measurements taken whenever I felt like it. Empty = not measured that day; don't carry the previous value forward.
doc.baseline: The first row ({date}) is the last measurement before the period, as a starting point.
doc.rule1: - **One row = one set.** Sets from the same day and routine make up the session.
doc.rule2: - **Weight in kg.** Barbell = total (bar + plates). Dumbbell = the weight of one. Machine and cable = what the machine shows.
doc.rule3: - **Type:** `{working}` counts toward progress; `{warmup}` doesn't; `{ramp} N` is approach step N before the working sets, with rising weight.
doc.rule4: - **Empty cells:** no weight and no reps = timed set (see `seconds`); no weight = bodyweight or reps only. Empty equipment = not logged.
doc.rule5: - **Empty routine** = free day, outside the routine.
doc.rule6: - **Note** = what I wrote about that set, as is.
doc.rule7: - **Rest:** worked out from the time of each set.
doc.rule8: - Date and time in my time zone ({timeZone}).

explore-programs-2.title: Publish and copy routines and programs
explore-programs-2.body: Your stuff is private now: publish whatever you want with the globe in the editor. In Explore, copy a whole program or a single routine, like it and share the link.

programs.title: Build your program and the app tells you what's up today
programs.body: Group your routines in the order you do them. When you open the app, Today shows you the next one and you start with one tap.

streak.title: Your streak per exercise
streak.body: Give your sets a range (for example 8–10). The flame counts the sessions in a row where you hit the top on all of them; tap it to see the exercise history and whether it's time to go up.

tiktok.title: Not sure how to do an exercise?
tiktok.body: While you train, tap the TikTok button and watch videos of that exercise without searching by hand.

export-for-ai.title: Export your history for your AI
export-for-ai.body: Pick a date range and share a file with your sets, routines and measurements. Give it to your AI and ask it to review your progress.

body-measurements.title: Log your measurements
body-measurements.body: Write down height, weight and body fat % with their date to see how you change. They go in the file you export, so your AI advises you better.

exercise-language.title: Exercises in English or Spanish
exercise-language.body: Choose how names show in your routines and your history in Profile → Settings. Search works with either.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: What data Gym Tracker keeps, what it uses it for, who sees it and how to delete your account.

sections.title: What we keep
items: Your account: email, username and your encrypted password (it is never stored as is). If you log in with Google, we get your name, your email and an identifier of your account from Google.
Your training: sets, routines, programs and the exercises you create.
If you add them: date of birth and measurements (height, weight and body fat %). They are health data, which is why they are optional.

On your phone: a cookie to keep you logged in, another with the interface language and, in the browser storage, the guided session in progress, the last equipment you used and the sets not sent yet. We don't use advertising or analytics cookies.

sections.title: What for
items: Only so the app works: showing your history, working out your streak and preparing the file for your AI when you ask for it. We don't sell your data or use it for advertising.

sections.title: Who sees it
items: Only you. The exception is what you decide to publish: that routine or program shows in Explore with your username, as it was when you published it, and other users can see it, like it and copy it. Nobody sees what you don't publish.
When you export your data for an AI, you share that file with whoever you choose.
To work, the app uses a server where the database lives, Cloudflare (which the site's traffic goes through) and Google (only if you log in with Google).

sections.title: How long
items: As long as you have your account. On top of that, a daily encrypted backup of the database is made, and each backup deletes itself after 90 days.

sections.title: Delete your account
items: From Profile → Settings → Delete my account. It is deleted instantly with everything of yours; it disappears from the backups within 90 days at most.
The exercises you created are deleted too, except the ones someone else uses: those stay in the catalog without your name.
Your publications are deleted with your account. The copies other people already made are theirs and they stay.

privacy.contact: To ask for a copy of your data, correct it or delete it, write to <email>{address}</email>.
